proposal.hypothesis: Increase only wheel_mass_kg by the advisory 0.014375 kg step from 0.03772512673560605 to 0.05210012673560605 while holding the round-4 geometry, actuation, and controller scales fixed. Expected mechanism: greater rotating mass raises the effective wheel axial inertia, so the same body angular-momentum disturbance requires a smaller wheel angular-velocity excursion, reducing the probability of hitting the 200 rad/s speed governor and lowering speed_governor_fraction below the 0.01 screening limit. Evidence for success would be a reduction in speed_governor_fraction without materially worsening the currently passing stability and drift metrics: status should remain completed, peak_tilt_deg should stay near or below 5 deg, final_1s_tilt_rms_deg near or below 2 deg, peak_pivot_displacement_mm near or below 2 mm, contact_fraction above 0.99, peak_slip_speed_m_s below 0.05 m/s, and continuous_torque_exceeded_fraction below 0.1. A regression in those metrics would indicate that the added rotating mass is coupling adversely into stability, pivot load, or torque demand rather than simply providing speed margin.
